Code-led is the only viable path without image generation. The replacement process requires five steps: name a unique mechanism and audience scene, list seven concrete visual systems, turn them into complete directions, run concept-seed with scope direction and mode Experience, and present the result via serve-question.

The agent prompt grants the agent autonomy to choose the world and strongest concept. Impeccable still requires probing once with the structured question tool. Concept-seed will run first, then the options will be presented via AskQuestion. Instrument Sans, Syne, and Space Grotesk are all banned by Impeccible.

Cabinet Grotesk, Clash Display, Satoshi, and Epilogue are viable alternatives to the banned fonts. Variable axes like opsz, wdth, and wght suit a magnet-style portfolio well. Bricolage Grotesque offers the most flexibility for width and weight manipulation.

Anybody, Recursive, and Schibsted Grotesk are also under consideration. Geist was ruled out because it lacks variable width axes.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The grounded list must be created before the typography portfolio prompt can be assigned. The brief pins typography-led decisions above random rolls.

Seven grounded directions will come from recruiter and creative-tech audiences, plus kinetic type traditions like Swiss posters and variable fonts. Tool monoculture is excluded. Letterforms carry identity, motion, and navigation as the interface. Candidate five is the assigned build.

The recruiter audience is defined as someone scanning a laptop between meetings, needing to find experience and projects quickly and remember the site an hour later. The two dominant category ruts are dark neon portfolios and maximal WebGL playgrounds. The first grounded candidate is the Type Specimen Drawer, modeled after open-type foundry specimen sheets with optical sizes and axis sliders as navigation.

The second candidate is the Swiss Poster Wall. It uses International Typographic Style grids and bleed type. The first viewport crops the name across a grid with Figma-style rulers.

The third candidate is the Variable Font Pressure Field. Cursor proximity drives weight and width per character. The first viewport shows the name as a live pressure field.

The fourth candidate is the Scroll Chapter Book of Type. Pinned chapters let words reflow and scrub between states. Experience becomes a type book.

Candidate five is the Spatial Letter Room. It treats display type as three-dimensional objects in space, driven by scroll cameras and HTML accessibility. The name extrudes into depth on the first viewport. The Index Card Spec Sheet is the sixth candidate, pairing fine-print specification grids with poster-scale type. The Ink Channel Sign idea was rejected as too close to the challenger category. The agent will sketch three concepts and select the strongest.

Kiln glaze shelves were rejected because decorative ceramics do not help recruiters find experience. ANSI BBS was also rejected due to terminal costumes and dark-tech vibes. Sneaker box stacks and darkroom ambience were weighed as alternatives but judged weaker for resume clarity and scanning.

Tropicalia collage was rejected because the brief bans portrait heroes. Desert neon was rejected as a neon and cream category costume. The agent extracted four design disciplines from the declined candidates: arrested-state discipline from kiln glaze, keyboard-first presence from ANSI BBS, deliberate scale mismatch from Tropicalia, and numbered chase sequences as timeline motion grammar from desert neon. It will now attempt to serve a question.

AskQuestion is unavailable. The agent will present the chosen direction directly in chat. It will infer the world from the brief alone only after probes fail or time out.

The agent will attempt serve-question with a schema flag first. If that fails, it will proceed directly with the assigned Spatial Letter Room, stating its assumptions. Because the brief pins typography-led decisions above random rolls, the agent can fuse the assigned spatial letter room with the typographic requirements from the brief.

The design read targets a solo developer portfolio for recruiters and hiring managers. It favors a kinetic, spatial typography language built around variable type, R3F MSDF text, and GSAP scroll choreography. Dials are set to high variance, high motion intensity, and low visual density. The world is named Letterfield, or alternatively Glyphfield. The raised Spatial Letter Room will pool one vermillion or copper accent once, inspired by the kiln glaze discipline.

Bricolage Grotesque from next/font/google will power the variable width and weight axes. The color palette rejects ink-and-lime, paper-and-cobalt, and purple AI tones. Education will appear as pullable index rows, and years will scramble as motion.
